title: Ops Helix cockpit: modular admin-utility hub and taskified runbook runtime
creator: Sarah Nguyen
description:
Background:
We have a growing number of small admin utilities, ad-hoc scripts, and runbook fragments used by SRE and Support. Current catalog is fractured (scripts in repos, ad-hoc Google Docs, and a few taskified runbooks). This causes: lack of provenance, inconsistent permissions, fragile ad-hoc remediation flows, and poor telemetry for RCA.

Proposal:
Build 'Ops Helix' — a modular cockpit that exposes a curated set of admin utilities and converts runbook fragments into composable, permissioned tasklets ("runlets") that can be executed from Console, CLI, or Slack. Key concepts: plugin-based runlets, typed inputs, dry-run/simulate mode, approval gating, observable execution traces (context snapshot + tokenized telemetry), RBAC-integrated execution, and audit log streaming to kinesis/stackdriver.

Core components to deliver in this ticket:
1) Runlet runtime: lightweight service that accepts a runlet manifest (yaml), validates inputs, enforces RBAC, executes steps with checkpoints, emits structured telemetry.
2) Cockpit UI surface: single-pane developer/operator view listing runlets with tags, last-run results, and one-click dry-run. (Low-fidelity wireframes linked below.)
3) CLI and Slack adapter: ability to invoke a runlet with typed params, receive progress updates, and require approval for high-risk steps.
4) Migration tooling: an importer that converts 1-2 canonical existing runbooks (support-hotfix, db-rollback) into runlets and registers them.
5) Observability and SLOs: dashboards showing runlet success-rate, median execution time, and most-common failure points; plus trace correlation with request_id and model_version.

Architecture notes:
- Runlets are executed in isolated ephemeral sandboxes (k8s Job with strict IAM role) with least-privilege credentials via short-lived tokens.
- Telemetry schema: structured JSON lines with fields {runlet_key, step_id, actor, request_id, model_version, input_hash, result_summary, duration_ms, exit_code}.
- Approvals: small workflow using existing approvals service; approval step can be auto-granted for P2 tasks, manual for P0.
- Safety: every runlet must implement a "preview" mode returning diffs for mutations; destructive steps require two-step confirmation.

Acceptance criteria (must be all green to move to "Done"):
- Runlet runtime deployed to staging and can run sample runlet that executes 3 steps with checkpoints.
- RBAC enforcement works end-to-end (user without role cannot trigger protected runlet).
- Dry-run returns deterministic preview output without side effects for two sample runlets.
- Slack adapter posts start/finish and stream of step updates to a #ops-runlets channel with links to Console trace.
- Migrated two canonical runbooks and validated end-to-end execution and telemetry ingestion into dashboards.
- Documentation: runlet manifest spec, runbook authoring guide, and operational runbooks for recovering failed runlets.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (this ticket): runtime + CLI + Slack + migrate 2 runbooks to staging; basic dashboard.
- Phase 1: integrate Console UI and approvals, expand to 10 curated runlets, run internal training session.
- Phase 2: open catalog to wider internal teams, automated onboarding for new runlets, policy-driven linting.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: runaway destructive runlet invoked accidentally. Mitigate: default to dry-run, require dual-approval for destructive tags, rate-limit runlets per team.
- Risk: credential exposure. Mitigate: short-lived credentials, recorded ephemeral sessions, no raw secrets in logs.
- Risk: unstructured telemetry. Mitigate: enforce schema and strict typed outputs for steps.

Links & artifacts:
- Low-fi wireframes: https://drive.google.com/ops-helix/wireframes (internal)
- Runlet manifest RFC: https://confluence.re/redwood/ops-helix-runlet-rfc
- Example migrated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-helix/pull/42 (draft)

comments: 2026-03-02 - Sarah Nguyen: Kickoff sync went well — Eng + SRE + Support aligned on core goals. Decided to keep runlet manifests intentionally small to avoid YAML explosion. Agreed to pilot with 2 high-value runbooks.

2026-03-04 - Mateo Ruiz: Initial prototype of runtime emits telemetry and stores traces in ops-traces. Found a permissions gap when trying to run DB-rollback; need a short-lived role for runlets that touch prod DB (workaround documented).

2026-03-07 - Priya Kumar (SRE): Reviewed manifest RFC — suggested adding 'impact_score' field to surface risk in the cockpit UI. Also requested explicit 'safe_mode' boolean on runlets that default to dry-run unless escalated.

2026-03-10 - Mateo Ruiz: Pushed draft PR for runtime (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-helix/pull/42). Unit tests for dry-run mode included. Need review from security for credential exchange flow.

2026-03-11 - Security (A. Lopez): Quick read — credential exchange approach acceptable if we use KMS-backed ephemeral tokens and rotate every 10m. Marked security_review_required=true. Full review in next sprint.

2026-03-12 - Sarah Nguyen: Milestone check: runtime deployed to staging, Slack adapter posting to #ops-runlets, migrated support-hotfix runbook and validated dry-run preview. Next: finish approval integration and grafana dashboard.
